posts.author: NovaFanPixel
AbigailFanAlready
posts.body:
NEW ACCOUNT JUST TO POST IN THIS THREAD I'M NOT KIDDING

Abigail (Saturn12 in-game btw) is exactly what this kind of squad needed. She's the only one who isn't dropping IQ for the bit and she still has the best comedic timing in the whole class. The "Oh yeah, they're loud, annoying… Retards?" deadpan at the vending machine had me ROFL. cool, funny, relatable, loyal, best girl of 2013, I'm not making it up.

[b]Now let's talk about the FINISHER. because somebody at Burst drew that.[/b]

let me actually walk through the frame work:

[list]
[*][b]frame 1[/b] — she's launching off the moving cart, hook fires off-screen first (that's the BANG you hear before you see her), gas line venting in a sharp downward burst that you can read as a tiny silhouette
[*][b]frame 2-4[/b] — she's airborne, full body rotation through the camera-whip, her hair is animated separately from her uniform from her grapple line, three layers of motion happening at once, all individually drawn
[*][b]frame 5[/b] — the flame guns blades start glowing that orange-yellow ignition. that's a CUSTOM color pass for her specifically. Grayson's Crucible glow is red-orange. Abigail's is gold-orange. the show is COLOR-CODING the girls' weapon energy so it reads instantly different from the boys' even in chaotic frames
[*][b]frame 6-8[/b] — she plants the hook on the open body, dives in, and the slashes are drawn as overlapping continuous arcs instead of standard impact frames. that's MORE work, not less. that's somebody saying "Abigail's kill cam will not look like Grayson's"
[*][b]frame 9[/b] — the explosion, but the camera holds on HER body language: she can't find a clean landing area, she rolls instead of sticking the landing, dirt in her hair. it's the most lived-in finisher animation I've seen all year
[*][b]and then the moment that broke me[/b] — mid-fall, she clutches her blue necklace pendant subconsciously, lands, then realizes it's still there, and SIGHS. quietly. that's a personal beat carved into a kill cam. you don't draw that unless you're writing her like a person.
[/list]

that's not just sakuga budget. that's somebody at the script + storyboard layer going "Abigail isn't decoration, she's the one who finishes the fight, and she gets ONE small private gesture inside the loudest moment of the episode." that's [b]Natsuki Takuya's[/b] whole philosophy on writing women in one shot — loud combat, quiet interior life, no fan-service framing, the camera respects her even in motion.

compare that to how a generic 2013 action-anime would have drawn this same moment: low-angle skirt shot during the air rotation, dramatic chest pant after landing, breathy "...did I do that?" line read. Burst drew the OPPOSITE of that, deliberately. the camera stays at her face. the necklace clutch is the emotional payoff, not her body.

"...How did that happen?" hits 10x harder when you realize the storyboard team made a CHOICE to give her that line at that angle.

I might be biased. I might be VERY biased. I do not care. Hanazawa was BORN to voice this character.
posts.editReason: typo, fixed her in-game name (Saturn12 not Saturn-12). also added the frame breakdown because I rewatched the cut 6 more times.

posts.author: KaichouEnjoyer
posts.body:
Miyuki getting the "no fear, no hesitation, no regrets" speech AT THE START of episode 1 is wild.

Most shows would save that for ep 6 minimum. Then the way she just smugly chooses Void Rift like "so is grass green then?" and Echo, Likko, Kieran and William all confirm one by one while their player count rolls 1,284 → 1,347... that's such a cool way to show "this is a different team, they're already a unit."

[b]The animation on her speech alone needs a separate award category.[/b] let me try to actually describe it:

Burst doesn't do the easy thing here. they don't push in for a close-up. they don't tilt the camera up to make her look bigger. they HOLD ON A WIDE THE WHOLE TIME and let her stillness do the work. the only thing that moves for the first three lines of her speech is her HAIR — individually animated against the data tower wind — while her body stays completely composed. then when she hits "[i]If the walls above stand in front of you, advance to crush them![/i]" the camera ALMOST imperceptibly drops by maybe 2-3 pixels per second, building a slow looming effect WITHOUT cutting. that's a hand-drawn camera move done with care over a full 8-second hold. that's effort. that's a key animator going "no, this is the shot, we're not cheating it with a still."

and her body language at "[i]Therefore, our choice towards history is refusal![/i]" — she doesn't raise her voice, she LOWERS it, while the OST swells underneath. she crosses her arms more tightly. the smug "so is grass green then?" frown softens at the corner of her mouth for ONE FRAME. that's the kind of micro-expression you draw on purpose. that's a character animator who studied her.

this is exactly what [b]Natsuki Takuya[/b] is known for in the original manga: women whose authority comes from stillness, not from being framed as "intimidating." Burst translated that to anime with FULL respect for the source.

"Those pigs can have whatever's left." Excuse me?? Class president of all time. I'm calling it: we are getting a Council vs Main Crew arc and I am READY. and when Miyuki finally goes off in combat, given how restrained they're drawing her right now, the eventual release is going to be NUCLEAR.

Also "Barbaracy" might be the funniest fake-formal word an anime has ever invented. Abigail's whole face turning into spiritual disgust was peak comedic timing — and crucially, the animators drew BOTH girls full-frame in that beat, no cheating with off-screen reactions. they wanted you to see both performances at once.

posts.author: HollowToast
posts.body:
Just finished the raw at 11pm UK time and I'm WIDE awake. This thread is moving way too fast, I had like 60 unread replies in the time it took me to make tea.

The KO/HEGG headquarters scene with Gamlet and Nova was such a tone shift. I genuinely thought we were getting a comfy office-banter scene about coffee and then Nova just goes "Currently the amount is 9,994" and the player counter on the wall starts ticking down in real time. 9,995. 9,994. 9,993. Anyone else cackle at "Can you bet at least fifty-five dollars this time?" lmaoooo Gamlet is such a loser, I love him already.

also — [b]Nova is animated with so much restraint and it kills me.[/b] the way she walks into that scene carrying the coffee tray, you'd think she'd just be a "support character" type framing. but watch her face during "Currently the amount is 9,994" — she doesn't look at Gamlet. she looks at the wall display. one beat. ONE beat of her eyes lingering on the counter ticking down. and the animator drew it so her shoulders barely fall like 1-2 pixels. she's TIRED. she's BEEN tired. they animated grief in posture, not in dialogue. that's how Natsuki Takuya writes women in the manga — the emotional weight is in the body, not in the lines. Burst's adaptation is HONORING that.

and then "Did you put honey in here?" / "Well, I always knew you liked it, so." — Yui Ishikawa's voice barely moves. the corner of Nova's mouth softens just enough for the lighting on it to change. that's a hand-drawn lighting pass on a 0.4 second beat between two stoic characters. you can see somebody at Burst going "this matters to the show. spend the time."

Then Nova says "It's over" with no music and that landed harder than any jumpscare this season. This either is genius or a mess and I'm here for either outcome.

Right. Bed. See you all on page 14 tomorrow.

posts.author: KagemitsuRespecter_2010
posts.body:
I am going to write the post nobody else seems ready to write yet:

[b]Miyuki Kagemitsu is the strongest character introduction of fall 2013.[/b] not "for a girl." not "for a rival." just strongest. period. and the show didn't even need to give her a fight scene to prove it.

think about what she does on screen in ep 1:

[list]
[*]she's introduced PRACTICING Zantetsuken in the lobby while firing into wall targets at the SAME time. that's her training montage and her character intro merged into one shot. nobody else gets that.
[*]she runs an entire student council squad and they CONFIRM Void Rift one by one BEHIND her. that's not a rival. that's a captain.
[*]"so is grass green then?" — one line and she dismisses the entire division choice debate that took the boys two minutes to argue.
[*]"those pigs can have whatever's left." — she looks DOWN at the main squad. she literally has a platform above them. the show is staging her higher than the protag.
[*]and then the THESIS SPEECH. in a tutorial lobby. before any fight. before Sora has even mastered burst step. she gets the speech of the season, in episode one, with no setup.
[/list]

if you put that introduction on a male character we'd all be calling him the lead. let's not pretend otherwise. Miyuki is being written with lead-level weight and Burst is animating her like one. Saori Hayami knows. the storyboard knows. we should all know.

respecting Miyuki Kagemitsu in this thread is the bare minimum. let her cook.

posts.author: SakugaThreadZero
posts.body:
I've been re-watching the episode for the third time tonight and I want to make this thread before it gets buried. Sorry mods, this is gonna be long. [b]The animation on the girls in this episode is so deliberately done that I have to write it out.[/b]

Because here's the thing: 2013 anime has a default mode for drawing female characters in action shows, and Burst [i]refused[/i] all of it. that's not me projecting. that's frame work. let me prove it.

[b]1. MIYUKI — "intimidation drawn through stillness"[/b]

her lobby intro is a single sustained shot of her practicing Zantetsuken while shooting wall targets. most studios would CUT this. fast cuts, hype angles, low-up shots. Burst draws her in a SINGLE WIDE HOLD where her body never breaks composure. the only motion is her sword arm and her hair. then she STOPS — "pausing like she's still deciding which side of the world she wants to stand on" — and Burst HOLDS the hold even longer. that's a key animator confident enough to bet that her stillness will sell the character harder than choreography would.

her speech at the end of the lobby crowd? same trick. wide composition, locked camera, hair animated separately, micro-camera-drift downward by maybe 2-3 pixels over the full 8-second hold to build looming without cutting. that takes SO much more work than a normal hype zoom. somebody at Burst studied her in the manga and translated her power as "the room moves around her, she doesn't move."

[b]2. ABIGAIL — "agency in the kill cam"[/b]

her finisher on YAMAGA284 is the headline sakuga of the episode and I want to make sure people don't reduce it to "cool grapple shot." here's what's actually happening:

[list]
[*]her flame guns blades glow gold-orange. Grayson's Crucible Blades glow red-orange. they custom-toned the girls' weapon energy to read distinct from the boys' even in chaos — that's a separate color pass at the comp layer
[*]her air-rotation through the camera-whip has THREE independent motion layers (body, hair, uniform skirt) all individually drawn instead of cel-shifted as one block. that's a real key animator's pass, not a cheat
[*]her slashes are drawn as continuous overlapping arcs instead of standard impact stamps. that's an EXTRA layer of in-betweens
[*]her landing is NOT a heroic stick — she can't find clean footing and rolls instead. somebody drew her landing badly on purpose because that's [i]truer[/i]
[*]and then the necklace pendant clutch — subconscious grab during the fall, lands, realizes it's still there, sighs relief. THAT IS A PRIVATE GESTURE INSIDE A KILL CAM. you don't draw that unless you respect the character as a person
[/list]

compare to how 99% of 2013 action shows would draw this finisher: low-angle skirt shot during the air rotation, dramatic chest pant after landing, breathy "...did I do that?" line read at half volume. Burst drew the EXACT OPPOSITE of that, on purpose. the camera respects her even mid-motion. "...How did that happen?" hits 10x harder when you realize they CHOSE that line read at that angle.

[b]3. LIKKO — "comedy drawn full-bodied"[/b]

Likko's lobby cameo is 4 seconds long and somebody at Burst gave it a FULL key-frame pass. she's dancing emotes and five random players start copying her — FIVE separately animated NPCs all matching her rhythm, not loop-recycled. that's a hand-drawn crowd reaction shot for a 4-second beat that 99% of studios would have done as a static crowd cut. and then her "Just start already!" before the Void Rift confirmation has a full chibi-style impatient stomp animation. Ayane Sakura's energy got drawn into the lines, you can see it.

that's how Natsuki Takuya draws Likko in the manga — she's the squad's chaos engine and the panels never deflate her energy for plot convenience. Burst kept that. they could've shrunk her into a one-line cameo. they didn't.

[b]4. ECHO — "drawn in motion, not in poses"[/b]

Echo's lobby intro is parkour jumps between two training rails while testing dual blades. her ENTIRE introduction is movement. she never stops moving. Burst is telegraphing her character through pure kinetic energy. and crucially, the parkour is drawn cleanly — clean weight transfer, real momentum, no impossible mid-air pivots to make her look more "graceful." she's drawn like an athlete, not a model.

Rina Satou's "confirmed. Void Rift." in the squad confirmation is delivered while she's leaning over the rail grinning. the animators specifically drew her body angled OUT — over the railing, into the scene — because Takuya writes Echo as the one who LEANS IN to things. that's character through staging, not exposition.

[b]5. NOVA — "grief drawn in posture"[/b]

Nova walks into the KO HQ scene carrying a coffee tray. that's it. that's the entire physical setup. and what Burst chose to animate is her shoulders. specifically, the way they barely fall — like 1-2 pixels — when she looks at the player counter ticking down from 9,995 to 9,994. she doesn't react to Gamlet's joke. she looks at the wall. she's been tired for a while. Burst drew the EXHAUSTION into her body language because Takuya writes Nova's grief as posture, not lines.

and the honey-in-the-coffee beat? Yui Ishikawa's voice barely moves and the corner of Nova's mouth softens just enough that the LIGHTING on it changes. they did a custom lighting pass on a 0.4 second emotional beat between two stoic characters. that's effort spent on quiet.

[b]so what's the pattern.[/b]

across all five women in episode 1, Burst made the same set of choices:

[list]
[*]extra in-between frames where most studios would cut
[*]private gestures embedded INSIDE loud moments instead of next to them
[*]cameras that respect bodies in motion (no skirt shots, no chest-pant holds, no fan-service framing)
[*]custom color and lighting passes for emotional beats that "didn't need" them
[*]stillness over hype-cuts for authority characters (Miyuki, Nova)
[*]full-bodied comedy animation for chaos characters (Likko, Abigail's vending machine deadpan)
[/list]

posts.author: Crucible_Igniter_42

[quote=HypeBeam_3500 — #62 (this page)]TEAM GRAYSON / TEAM SORA / TEAM ABIGAIL[/quote]

okay I'll bite. [b]TEAM GRAYSON[/b] and I will FIGHT in this thread.

real talk: Grayson's contribution to that fight is the MOST IMPRESSIVE work in the entire sequence. Abigail's finisher is the headline sakuga, sure. but Grayson was doing CHESS in the middle of a knife fight. let me show you.

watch the fight again. zero in on Grayson. the man is fighting THREE enemies at once: YAMAGA284 on the front, plus the two flanking attackers. and what does he do? he doesn't [i]try[/i] to kill any of them. he HERDS them. one Crucible Blade circles HIGH like a predator wing. the other carves LOW in hard vector lines. that's not attacking. that's POSITIONING. every blade pass forces the enemy team into worse footing.

and the choreography is INSANELY readable. Grayson is the more agile one. YAMAGA284 is the weight. Grayson opens lanes with a glove flick. YAMAGA cashes them in with a shoulder-ram or a point-blank gun. they're a TWO-MAN UNIT in the choreography for the first half of the fight, and Grayson is the one DRIVING the rhythm. one drives. the other makes it hurt.

then comes IGNITION mode. flames race through the channels with that deep [i]fwoomph[/i] ignition sound. heat distortion ripples the comp layer. and Grayson's flaming blades stop just intercepting and start FORCING the enemy line into bad footing. you can SEE him processing the battle in real time. one enemy dives high — Grayson plants a foot, vaults over YAMAGA's shoulder, rotates through the air in a long readable arc, one blade rising with him, the other carving low across the grass — AND FOR TWO FRAMES THE WHOLE IMPACT COLLAPSES INTO SILHOUETTE. black, white, orange. THEN snaps back into full color as steel hits, sparks burst, attacker is cut sideways out of the air. lands in a low three-point skid, dirt kicking under his hand, snaps back up before the camera fully catches him.

and then the moment that I will be thinking about for WEEKS: a sniper round cracks toward him. he tilts JUST ENOUGH for it to miss. catches the NEXT shot on the FLAT of a returning blade. [b]AND GRINS through the spark shower.[/b]

THAT is the coolest moment in the episode. it's not even close. fight me.

and the kicker: Grayson doesn't take the kill. he doesn't NEED to. he stepped BACK and let Sora go 1v1 with YAMAGA because that's what the squad needed. that's not "letting his friend have it." that's a tactical decision by a guy who already had the fight WON. he was always going to be the one who could close it. he chose NOT to. that's a lead-tier fight beat in a SIDE CHARACTER'S first action scene.

posts.author: RedHairedHeroines_4Eva
posts.body:
okay I want to articulate the thing this thread keeps circling but not quite saying out loud:

[b]the reason Eden ep 1 hit this hard is because of how it writes its women.[/b]

not in addition to the action. not in spite of the action. [i]because of[/i] it.

compare to literally any "trapped-in-VR" anime from the last three years. the formula is: male protag struggles + male rival exposits + female love interest worries + female support archetype heals + female antagonist seduces. you can map every show in this genre onto that grid in 30 seconds.

now run the grid on Eden ep 1:

[list]
[*]female protagonist-tier authority figure: [b]Miyuki.[/b] she gets the thesis speech.
[*]female rival/parallel: [b]Echo Desmond.[/b] she gets motion as character intro.
[*]female love interest: [i]NOT IN THIS EPISODE.[/i] no girl is introduced through romantic gaze.
[*]female support archetype: [i]NOT IN THIS EPISODE.[/i] no girl is reduced to healer/cheerleader.
[*]female antagonist seductress: [i]NOT IN THIS EPISODE.[/i] Likko taunts but it's COMPETITIVE not sexual.
[*]female strategic anchor: [b]Lisa[/b] AND [b]Sarah.[/b]
[*]female senior authority: [b]Nova.[/b]
[*]female finisher: [b]Abigail.[/b]
[/list]

the show CONSCIOUSLY refused to fill the four most common "female anime archetype" slots and instead filled SEVEN different lead-coded slots with women. that's a design document choice. somebody in pre-production drew up the cast and said "no, this isn't going to be like the other VR shows."

that's what makes ep 1 feel different. that's the secret. the fight choreography is great. the music is great. but the THING people feel and can't name is that this might be the first time in years a fall premiere refused to put its female characters into the standard slots. [b]they all lead something.[/b]

Burst is doing the right thing. Takuya wrote them this way. Kisaragi adapted them with no concessions. Suzuhara boarded them like leads. let's give them a fall season for it.

posts.author: MetaCode_Maximus
posts.body:
[quote=Crucible_Igniter_42 — #66 (this page)]TEAM GRAYSON. I'll die on this hill.[/quote]

absolutely not. I read every word of your essay. respect the writeup. I disagree on every single line.

[b]TEAM SORA.[/b] let me make the case.

Grayson had the highest TECHNICAL ceiling in the fight, sure. cool blade work. flame ignition. sniper-deflect-grin. I see it. I respect it. but the EMOTIONAL CORE of that fight was Sora, and the show KNOWS it. Burst knew it. the camera knew it. the storyboard knew it. that's why [b]the fight doesn't go 1v1 until SORA forces it.[/b]

let me walk you through the most important beat in that fight, which @Crucible_Igniter_42 is conveniently ignoring:

Grayson is mid-fight. doing his herding choreography. KILLING it. and Sora — the WEAKEST member of the squad with the LEAST mastered weapon — turns AROUND mid-cart-escape and RUNS BACK toward YAMAGA. with the blade-arm only. no bullet mastery. no burst step mastery. just SPITE and a sharp object.

"[i]Grayson! Let me have a go![/i]"
"[i]Piss off![/i]"
"[i]Argh...!!![/i]"

that's not heroic. that's STUPID. and the show frames it that way. Grayson is irritated. he LEAVES because Ben is screaming about the cart. Grayson PEELS OFF. and now Sora has to fight YAMAGA284 ALONE.

what happens next is character work disguised as choreo. Sora gets CUT. like, blood-on-the-grass cut. he gets shoulder-checked across the field. BAM. he rolls. spits blood. pushes himself up. no speech. JUST BREATHING.

and then he STARTS LEARNING. the READ LEVEL on YAMAGA284 ticks down in real time: [b]100% → 82% → 70% → 55% → 30%[/b] as he stops doing the same approach over and over. he WATCHES the UI in real time. that's a 12-year-old kid noticing the system and ADAPTING to it inside a fight he's not winning.

then MetaCode AWAKENS more. the plates flicker. ports open. red pulse through the seams. Sora sees it happen in real time. "[i]What!?[/i]" the burst step UNLOCKS. he doesn't celebrate. he just USES it. unmastered. ugly. SHAKY. fwip — he vanishes sideways in a red-metal speed burst. not mastered. not elegant. but real. appears at YAMAGA's flank, eyes widened just slightly, then dashes in and punches HARD.

"[i]NOW!!!![/i]" — SMASH.

that's the moment YAMAGA284 stops being the boss and starts being a body that can be killed.

Abigail closes it. Grayson set it up. but SORA EARNED IT. he turned a 1v1 he couldn't win into a 1v1 he could SET UP for somebody else to finish. that's a protag arc inside a single fight in EPISODE ONE.

also — and this matters — Mariya Ise's "AAARRGGHHHH!!!" charge is the vocal performance of the season. you can HEAR the exhaustion underneath the rage. that's not a power-up scream. that's a kid who's already tired and forcing himself to keep going. that's the heart of the whole show in one line read.

he didn't get the kill. but he made it possible. the show TELLS YOU SO. Sora stands there breathing hard, blade lowered, staring at the body. [i]"That matters more."[/i] — literally a narration line. the show is TELLING you whose fight that was.

@Crucible_Igniter_42 your boy did chess work. respect. but Sora fought the fight that ACTUALLY happened.

[b]TEAM SORA.[/b] and yeah Abigail's finisher is sick. but Sora made the finisher POSSIBLE.

posts.author: Council1_Forever
posts.body:
I want to use my post slot to lock in [b]Likko Valenne[/b] and [b]Echo Desmond[/b] appreciation because they are getting flattened into "antagonist support girls" and I will NOT have it.

[b]LIKKO VALENNE (Hammond Council 1, Secretary — Ayane Sakura)[/b]

Likko is on screen for less than a minute total in ep 1 and Burst gave her THREE distinct character beats:

[list]
[*][b]Lobby intro[/b] — she's dancing emotes and five separate NPCs are individually animated copying her rhythm. that's a hand-drawn crowd reaction shot. for FOUR SECONDS. that's somebody at Burst going "Likko's chaos energy moves rooms." rooms move WITH her.
[*][b]Pre-Void Rift confirmation[/b] — "just start already!" with full chibi-style impatient stomp animation. Ayane Sakura voicing impatience that hits like comedic violence. in the same lobby where Miyuki is delivering THE speech, Likko's the one cutting through with one impatient line.
[*][b]Montage shotgun blast taunt[/b] at the end — she fires AND taunts AT THE SAME TIME. zero hesitation. one-handed shotgun. that's not "support antagonist." that's an action lead with a comedy filter.
[/list]

Likko is not the squad's mascot. she's the squad's pressure release. she's the reason Council 1 reads as a UNIT instead of as Miyuki + four background avatars. she's holding her own.

[b]ECHO DESMOND (Hammond Council 1, VP — Rina Satou)[/b]

Echo is introduced through pure motion. her ENTIRE intro is parkour between two training rails while testing dual blades. she never stops moving. and the parkour is drawn cleanly — real weight transfer, real momentum, no impossible mid-air poses. she's drawn like an athlete who has BEEN here, not like a character being introduced.

and Rina Satou's "confirmed. Void Rift." in the squad confirmation? delivered while she's leaning OVER the rail grinning. Burst staged her body angled INTO the scene, not posed away from it. that's a girl who LEANS IN to things. that's storytelling through staging.

Echo is the VICE PRESIDENT of Hammond Council 1. her body language right now is more aligned with Miyuki than any of the boys are with Sora. that's foreshadowing. Echo is going to be Miyuki's right hand in actual command moments and we're going to feel it.

[b]summary:[/b] Council 1's five named members are Miyuki (President), Echo (VP), William (Supervisor), Kieran (Advisor), Likko (Secretary). THREE of those five are women, and Burst is animating all three of them with distinct, deliberate, character-first choices. that's not "the boys' rival squad has some girls in it." that's "the squad is LED and STRUCTURED by women, the boys are the support staff."

respect Likko. respect Echo. they're carrying Council 1 with Miyuki, not behind her.

I want to push back on the early-thread takes that read Nova and Gamlet as a "shipping" scene. that's flattening her and I'm not having it.

watch the coffee beat again. Gamlet says "did you put honey in here?" and Nova answers "well, I always knew you liked it, so." if you're going to ship them — fine, it's the internet — at least ship her UP not sideways. Nova is not "Gamlet's anything." Gamlet is "Nova's boss in name only." that's the dynamic. write it correctly.

posts.author: EchoDesmond_VP4Life
posts.body:
EST trash here. it's 4am, I just rewatched ep 1 for the third time, and I have to write the Echo Desmond post nobody is writing yet. she is being treated as "the third girl on Council 1" and she is so much MORE than that. let me cook.

[b]ECHO DESMOND — HAMMOND COUNCIL 1 VICE PRESIDENT — VA: RINA SATOU[/b]

[b]1. Introduction as motion.[/b] we meet Echo while she is parkouring between two training rails testing dual blades. Burst did not introduce her standing still. they did not introduce her in a static portrait. they introduced her IN motion. that's not just a stylistic flex — that's the show telling you "this character's identity is movement." she does not exist as a pose. she exists as a verb.

[b]2. The parkour is animated CORRECTLY.[/b] weight transfers properly between her feet. her shoulders compensate for her hips. her hair physics lag a beat behind her head turns instead of moving in sync. her dual blades have separate motion arcs because she's HOLDING them, not posing with them. nobody at Burst said "let's make her look graceful." somebody said "let's make her look like an athlete." those are different objectives and the second one is harder.

[b]3. No fan-service framing during the parkour.[/b] camera is held at chest-height in three-quarter view. no low-angle. no zoom on legs. no skirt physics. she's wearing standard student-council gear with no costume tricks. Burst could have done the lazy thing and they refused. that's a deliberate storyboarding choice from [b]Tomoe Suzuhara[/b] and it's a CHOICE.

[b]4. Rina Satou's "Confirmed. Void Rift."[/b] two words. flat tone. no flirty lilt. no breathy delivery. just clipped pro-soldier confirmation while she's leaning over the rail grinning into the lobby. that's the same "I have done this a hundred times" energy you hear in a senior squad lead. Rina Satou is reading Echo as a VETERAN.

[b]5. Body language in the squad shot.[/b] Miyuki is in the center delivering the speech. Echo is staged DIRECTLY BEHIND her right shoulder. that's the "second-in-command" frame from any military or action genre. Burst put her there on purpose. she's the VP of Council 1 in fiction AND in staging.

[b]6. The dual blades.[/b] Echo's blades are smaller, lighter, paired weapons. Grayson gets long single Crucible blades. Abigail gets a grappling pistol. Miyuki gets Zantetsuken. each character's weapon is BUILT for their body and their movement style. Echo's weapon is built for SPEED and MOBILITY which matches her parkour intro. that's character design at the weapon level. nobody at Burst was lazy about Echo.

[b]7. The character grin.[/b] Rina Satou voices the small grin Echo gives during the lobby exposition. she's having FUN. she's not stressed. she's not nervous. she's not anxious about the upcoming match. she's amped. that's an athlete's pregame face. that's how you write a confident character without making her arrogant.

Echo Desmond is going to be the breakout of this season for anyone who wasn't already locked in on Miyuki or Abigail. Rina Satou + this design + this much motion attention = a character who's going to OWN her own action set piece by ep 4 or 5. plant this flag. quote me later.

respect Echo. she's earning it in every frame she's on screen and she's only been on screen for like 90 seconds.

posts.author: LisaSarah_Squad

okay before this page 5 turns into another "but Sora though" loop, I want to plant a flag for the girls who are NOT in fights this episode and are STILL doing the work:

[b]LISA NEMA-OYUNAA[/b] — the FIRST person in the classroom riot scene to [i]name[/i] what's actually happening. while everyone else is yelling, Lisa is the one who says "they're not playing fair, this isn't a fight, it's a SHOOT." she's diagnosing the situation in real time. that's a strategist brain. she's the one Ben goes to FIRST when he's spiraling, and she's the one who tells him sit down and breathe. Lisa is the squad's anchor and the show is already telling us so.

[b]SARAH[/b] — the second the cafeteria mob escalates Sarah is on her phone CALLING somebody. who is she calling? we don't know yet. but the staging shows her actively trying to fix the situation while two boys around her are yelling about how unfair it is. Sarah is doing crisis management at AGE TWELVE. and she does it without raising her voice. that's a lead-level character trait.

[b]ABIGAIL JUNE[/b] — everyone is talking (correctly) about her grapple finisher but I want to highlight her BEFORE the fight. Abigail is the one who walks INTO the school riot calm. she doesn't pick up a weapon, doesn't run away, doesn't escalate. she just [i]moves through it[/i] with her hands in her hoodie pockets. that staging is intentional. the chaos breaks AROUND her. Abigail is being drawn as un-rattle-able. THAT'S who you want anchoring your team. that's why the grapple finisher hit later — Burst already taught you in act 1 that Abigail is who stays calm when everyone else loses it.

three girls. zero major fight scenes between them in the first half of the episode. all three of them are STILL the most composed people on screen during the chaos. then Abigail goes on to end the YAMAGA fight.

this is what people mean when they say "Eden writes women like leads." it's not just the action beats. it's the WAY the camera trusts them to anchor scenes the boys are losing their minds in. Lisa thinks. Sarah acts. Abigail endures. and then ends the threat.

respect the sane girls. they're the spine of this team.

I'm saying it because Eden is clearly refusing the default action-anime arrangement where the boys drive the fight and the girls react prettily from the side. [b]We're not doing "male dominate, female support."[/b] not with this storyboard. not with this shot priority. not with Abigail getting the kill card.

let's actually break down what Abigail did. because she did NOT "show up at the end and take the cleanup." that's an INSULT to what's on screen. let me prove it.

[b]1.[/b] she SAW Sora turn back. she SAW Grayson peel off to help Ben with the cart. she SAW Sora's 1v1 with YAMAGA happening. she chose to LAUNCH from the moving cart that Grayson was driving for two minutes. read that again. she JUMPED OFF a moving vehicle in the middle of a war zone to back up a teammate. no hesitation. no setup line. she just SENT IT.

[b]2.[/b] her launch is one of the cleanest aerial transitions in the entire episode. flame guns grapple hook fires OFF-SCREEN first — you HEAR the bang before you see her — gas line venting in a sharp downward burst that reads as a tiny silhouette, full body rotation through the camera-whip, THREE independent motion layers (body, hair, uniform) all individually drawn instead of cel-shifted as one block. this is hand-drawn key animator showoff work. one continuous unbroken cut from launch to land. that's not "the cleanup." that's a sakuga signature moment.

[b]3.[/b] her finisher is a continuous unbroken cut from hook-plant to kill. NO cheat-cuts. plant the hook on the open body, dive in, slash with flame guns blades at NEAR-CONTACT range, blade glow custom-colored gold-orange (deliberately different from Grayson's red-orange so the audience can read who's killing who in the chaos), continuous overlapping slash arcs instead of standard impact stamps. YAMAGA's machine armor EXPLODES. BOOOM. red blood explodes out of the body. center-frame "[b]K.O![/b]" text. nobody else got a kill cam like that. she made YAMAGA [i]literally detonate[/i].

[b]4.[/b] THE NECKLACE CLUTCH DURING THE FALL. mid-air. subconscious grab. lands BADLY because the storyboard chose realism over heroism. dirt in her hair. uses the hook tension to yank herself around but can't find an area, so she just ROLLS onto the ground. then she NOTICES the necklace is still there and exhales relief. "[i]...How did that happen?[/i]" delivered like she didn't expect it to work. she COMMITTED to the finisher without knowing it would land. that's not "cleanup." [b]that's a leap of faith made in real time.[/b]

so let's correct the record:

[list]
[*]Grayson fought the middle of the fight. he didn't take the kill because he set up the squad.
[*]Sora fought the HEART of the fight. he set up the kill with raw spite.
[*][b]Abigail LED the ending of the fight.[/b] she didn't "assist." she made the decisive choice, jumped off a moving cart, performed the cleanest sakuga sequence of the episode, made YAMAGA's body literally detonate, AND committed to the move not knowing if she'd survive the landing.
[/list]

@Crucible_Igniter_42 chess work doesn't kill YAMAGA. chess work POSITIONS YAMAGA. she KILLED him.
@MetaCode_Maximus Sora set it up, true. but the finisher is what BURST chose to put their best key animator on. you can SEE the production hours in the cut. that's where the studio decided "this is the moment we are proud of."

the show literally TOLD YOU the answer with the shot list. Grayson's fight is wide-shot tactical choreography (cool). Sora's fight is mid-shot earn-the-hit progression (great). Abigail's kill is a CENTER-FRAME one-cut sakuga showcase with on-screen "K.O!" text and an explosion. the camera told you which moment Burst wanted you to remember.

and zoom out from the fight for two seconds: Miyuki gets the thesis speech. Nova gets the ominous "It's over" adult-world gravity. Likko gets a full-body comedy animation beat in four seconds. Echo is introduced through movement instead of posing. Abigail gets the finisher. Eden is building its female cast as engines, not ornaments. girls are not being carried by the plot. they are carrying the plot's pressure points.

that's why [b]TEAM ABIGAIL[/b] matters. it's not only "who looked coolest." it's the show proving its women can lead action, comedy, authority, horror, emotional restraint, and narrative payoff. maybe more than the men. maybe that's the whole point. and honestly? good. let them lead.

[b]TEAM ABIGAIL.[/b] coffin shut. mic dropped. necklace clutched. I'm putting flowers on YAMAGA284's grave.

(I am open to a TEAM TIE answer mechanically. but thematically? no. Abigail had the CLEANEST moment of the three and the girls are the core of this episode. that's the non-negotiable.)

got a few requests in PMs so I'm posting Miyuki's full lobby speech here for the database. this is the actual transcript pass, not a fan TL. corrections welcome but I'm fairly confident on this one:

[quote="Miyuki Kagemitsu — pre-Void Rift lobby speech, ep 1"]"[b]No fear, no hesitation, no regrets![/b]
[b]If the walls above stand in front of you, advance to crush them![/b]
[b]Restrictions behind history are merely an excuse to refuse living![/b]
[b]That is the real truth of humanity![/b]
[b]Because of our mistakes, we deserve a path to choose where we keep moving forward![/b]

I need everyone to understand: this is what gets BOOMED out IN THE LOBBY before anyone has even fought a boss. no buildup. no flashback. no slow camera push-in. she just delivers it — framing tight, music dropped to silence underneath, her voice swelling on every line break — and then immediately picks Void Rift like none of it cost her anything.

that "[i]our choice towards history is refusal[/i]" line is the show's thesis statement. mark it. that's going to be the line of the season.

posts.author: AW_Girls_Retrospective
posts.body:
before this thread closes I want to put one thing on permanent record for whenever someone digs this back up after ep 12 airs:

[b]this thread — all 56 pages, all 1,100+ posts, all four days of arguments and theories and shouting matches — was carried by appreciation for the women of Eden.[/b]

let me just list it back out for the historical record:

[list]
[*][b]page 1:[/b] AbigailFanAlready dropped a frame-by-frame breakdown of Abigail's grapple finisher within HOURS of the broadcast. KaichouEnjoyer wrote the first major Miyuki appreciation post on the same page. HollowToast pulled out Nova's posture work that early. day one this thread was already centered on the women.
[*][b]page 2:[/b] KagemitsuRespecter_2010 called Miyuki "the strongest character introduction of fall 2013, period, not for a girl, just strongest." SakugaThreadZero dropped the FULL women's animation essay running through all five named female characters at once. nobody was reducing them to side roles.
[*][b]page 3:[/b] Ishikawa_Disciple gave Nova her own marquee post. KaichouEnjoyer doubled down on Miyuki's micro-expressions. the FRM/KO theories that ended up being thread canon all came back through Nova's authority in the office scene.
[*][b]page 4:[/b] the YAMAGA debate. Team Grayson vs Team Sora vs Team Abigail. and Team Abigail kept WINNING the argument page after page. RedHairedHeroines_4Eva mapped the trope grid and proved Eden refused to fill the female archetype slots. Council1_Forever broke down how 3 of Council 1's 5 named members are women including President and VP. Nova_Is_The_Boss reframed Nova as the office's actual command center.
[*][b]page 5:[/b] GunKata_Saturn12 declared "we're not doing male dominate, female support" and made it the thread's thesis. EchoDesmond_VP4Life cooked Rina Satou's parkour intro at 4am EST. LisaSarah_Squad put Lisa Nema-Oyunaa and Sarah on the record as crisis-management leads. Donut_Punisher ended page 5 with "TEAM EDEN GIRLS LEADING THE SHOW."
[*][b]pages 6-50:[/b] the hype kept compounding. every page had at least one major girl-animation appreciation post. people kept finding new frames to admire. Miyuki/Abigail/Nova/Likko/Echo/Lisa/Sarah each got their own dedicated threads INSIDE the thread.
[*][b]this final page:[/b] we are still talking about them.
[/list]

I have been on YAL since 2011. I have seen a lot of fall premieres. I have seen a lot of episode 1 threads. [b]this is the first time I have watched a forum collectively refuse to flatten the female cast of a show into "side characters" in real time.[/b] Eden did the work. Burst did the work. Takuya wrote them this way. Suzuhara boarded them this way. Hayami/Hanazawa/Ishikawa/Satou/Sakura voiced them this way. and the THREAD responded in kind.

this is what "girls lead" looks like in fandom. it doesn't mean ignoring Sora or Ben or Grayson. it means you ALSO show up for Miyuki and Abigail and Nova and Likko and Echo and Lisa and Sarah, every page, every post, no matter how long the thread runs.

we did that here. proud of this forum.

see you all in the ep 2 thread Sunday night. and the ep 3. and every other thread for the next 12 weeks.

[b]TEAM EDEN GIRLS LEADING THE SHOW.[/b] roll credits.

posts.author: SakugaThreadZero
posts.body:
[b]ACTION DIRECTOR YUSUKE KAGURA IS A GOD. SAKUGA OF THE YEAR.[/b]

I just finished rewatching Grayson vs IgniteCOD_Clutch at 0.5x speed and I'm losing my mind. Look at the martial arts fundamentals Kagura put into Grayson's choreography: it's not generic floaty anime sword-flailing. It's grounded [b]BOXING JABS AND STREET KICKS[/b]:

[list]
[*]When Ignite slides, Grayson drops his hips and stamps a stiff low kick right into the knee to kill the slide.
[*]When Ignite tries to aim his SMG, Grayson delivers a sharp front kick to break his aim stance.
[*]When Ignite deploys a build panel for cover, Grayson doesn't waste magic — he plants his heel into a heavy, devastating axe kick that splits the panel in half!
[*]And that spinning back kick timed to Ignite's teleport exit... the anticipation animation was immaculate!
[/list]

He held the Crucible flames until the end like punctuation marks. Hands and kicks won the space — Crucibles cashed out the damage! And that three-frame impact hold on [i]Lethal Crucible: Red Divide[/i]? Absolutely unreal compositing from Studio Burst.

posts.author: IgniteCOD_Sweat
posts.body:
IgniteCOD_Clutch is literally every toxic Modern Warfare 2 sweat in existence lmfaoooo

The guy throws down launch pads, spams sticky mines, quickscopes with his rifle, and furiously rage-types in floating text chat: [i]"??? Who the f—? Get off me!"[/i] and [i]"Look at this, bitch!"[/i] with his drones out XD

And Grayson doesn't even say a word — he just walks straight through the gunfire with Gojo spacing arrogance and Ichigo forward pressure, breaks Ignite's machete with his bare boot, and Ignite's final dying message before dissolving into golden EXP is: [i]"damn... nice..."[/i]. Burst writers definitely play competitive multiplayer games, this parody was too accurate!

posts.author: NodeCorePilot
posts.body:
[b]BEN SMYTHE VS MAXINO WAS THE MANLIEST FIGHT OF 2013.[/b]

Maxino turning the entire circular fossil basin into an explosive firework minefield with delayed rockets and launch zones was crazy. But Ben's response?! Switching between Machine Gun to snipe missiles out of the air, Flight Mode to redirect the blast recoil, and Drill Mode to parry Maxino's shield!

And that 45-second Grand Finale countdown at the end: Ben is at 96% heat, coughing blood, Maxino yells [i]"You missed one!"[/i], and Ben just grins: [i]"Oh yeah!? You wish!"[/i] and [b]RUNS STRAIGHT INTO THE POINT-BLANK BLAST[/b]! The explosion catches his back, blood and sparks tear across the screen, and he drives that roaring NodeCore drill right through Maxino into the fossil ridge screaming: [b]"HERE'S YOUR L!"[/b]

Then collapsing face-first in the mud at 100% heat murmuring [i]"Scientific reaction..."[/i], whacking his smoking engine with a wrench, and getting right back up: [i]"You've got five more minutes in you. That wasn't a question."[/i] Ben is an absolute legend.

posts.author: SoraGauthier_Fanboy
posts.body:
Can we talk about how smart [b]Sora vs Nero[/b] was? Nero wasn't a brute boss, he was an analytical route-controller who used a 3-color lane system (blue = move, yellow = delay, red = punish). He wasn't tracking Sora's speed — he was tracking Sora's [i]habits[/i], counting on Sora's protective instinct to rush in whenever Abigail's route was threatened!

When Sora realizes that flash-stepping and rushing are giving Nero all his predictive data, he doesn't pull out a sudden power-up. He breaks the calculation by taking an [b]ordinary, human, pathetic step[/b]:

[quote="The tactical narration:"][i]"Nero's prediction was perfect. That was why it failed. It predicted the Sora who had already panicked. The Sora in front of him now had learned the cruelest survival lesson available: running and surviving are not the same action."[/i][/quote]

And look at the sheer kinetic grit right before that when Ben launches him in: Sora falls into the ground, rolls through the dirt to absorb the impact, immediately pushes back up, and charges straight into Nero without losing an ounce of momentum. It wasn't played for laughs at all — you can feel his raw determination to close the distance!

Then shattering the route line beneath Nero's feet, making the cat-ears face, tapping his forehead with the 'L' sign, whispering [i]"Later~"[/i] and blitzing away! Mariya Ise brought so much charisma to that sequence :3

posts.author: AbigailFanAlready
posts.body:
[b]ABIGAIL VS MIYUKI WAS PURE UNFILTERED HATRED.[/b]

Zero friendly anime tournament vibes. Look at the dialogue when their weapons locked:

[quote="Duel Dialogue:"][b]Abigail:[/b] "Miyuki, it's been 6 years and you're still hurting everyone! Stop doing this!"
[b]Miyuki:[/b] "And that's the problem! You're acting as if there are rights to rebel against authority!"
[b]Abigail:[/b] "This isn't about school, it's about you!"
[b]Miyuki:[/b] "Do not tell me what to do, you lower caste pig!"
[b]Abigail:[/b] "Fine then! I'll push it through your brain, b**ch!"[/quote]

Kana Hanazawa and Saori Hayami were screaming with so much venom! And the choreography: Flame Guns vs Zantenzetsuken. When Abigail caught the blade, pulled herself in with the hook cable, and delivered that brutal spin-kick into Miyuki's guard — the camera zoomed in on Miyuki's forearm trembling from adrenaline and pain. First time in the whole anime Miyuki's composure broke!

posts.author: LisaSniperQueen
posts.body:
[b]ECHO VS LISA WAS CATFIGHT OF THE DECADE!![/b]

First Lisa interrupts Margo's screaming sound cannon: [i]"You're mine, pig!!"[/i] — Rina Satou delivering that line gave me actual chills. But then Echo Desmond drops in with that absurd [b]Anchor Armament[/b] — dual blades that transform into twin rotary machine guns, and then combine into that massive double-edged Anchor Greatsword!

And their dialogue while trading lethal strikes was so petty and hilarious:

Echo: [i]"Aww, is that your toy to feel important?"[/i]
Lisa: [i]"Enough hiding behind the Council!"[/i]
Echo: [i]"Congratulations. You got the whole school laughing! Hahahahaha! Burn in h**l!"[/i]
Lisa: [i]"...You pig."[/i]
Echo: [i]"I'm staring at how UGLY your shoes look."[/i]
Lisa: [i]"Nobody cares! Garbage!!"[/i]

And they literally ended the clash by double drop-kicking each other across the arena! Need their rematch animated immediately.

posts.author: 3EpisodeRule
posts.body:
[b]3-Episode Test Verdict: AOTS CONTENDER.[/b]

Look at the variety of combat styles in this single episode:

[list]
[*]Grayson: Pure boxing footwork, checking slides with low kicks, axe kicks, Gojo spacing arrogance
[*]Ben: High-risk heat management, point-blank explosions, NodeCore drill power
[*]Sora: Route reading, patience under pressure, ordinary human step counterplay
[*]Abigail: Aggressive Flame Gun rushdown & hook line mobility
[*]Lisa: Cold tactical focus scan & terrain denial
[*]Minko: Slapstick momentum & accidental physics parries
[/list]

Nobody fights the same way. Every character has a completely distinct physical identity. Burst debut of the decade!

posts.author: SoraGauthier_Fanboy
posts.body: Sora vs Nero was a psychological battle disguised as an action sequence. Nero's 3-lane route grid (blue = move, yellow = delay, red = punish) wasn't just a boss gimmick; Nero was literally reading player psychology. He counted on Sora's shounen instinct to rush in whenever someone yelled.

posts.author: Andreas_VectorUplink
posts.body: Likko running down the wall like an elegant classical ballerina with her rhythm shotgun to fast piano music ('4e corde! Tempo miracle ultra-rapide!')... only for Minko to get caught in the route wheel, spin 360 degrees, get catapulted across the canyon into a tree, chase the cart on foot, and whack Grayson in the back of the head with her scythe handle: 'OW! DAMMIT, MINKO!'

posts.author: EchoDesmond_Loyalist
posts.body: Emiko calling Arthur White 'Whitie~ You there~?' in the post-credits scene! She's the acting CEO of FRM while casually walking a fashion show in Shell 2?! The lore rabbit hole goes so deep.

posts.author: Grayson_Ignition_DualBlades
posts.body: Look at the weight in Sora's landing when Ben launches him in — he hits the ground, tucks into a combat roll, pushes right back up to his feet without losing speed, and charges Nero head-on. Sora's scrappy physical combat style is so satisfying to watch!

posts.author: GraysonSus_NotSus
posts.body: Kagura holding back the Crucible flames until the very end — hands and kicks win the space, Crucibles cash out the damage! That Red Divide cut splitting the corridor in two with that delayed three-frame impact hold... Kagura is an animation god.

posts.author: Nishikawa_OP_Hype
posts.body: The animation when Sora realizes flash-stepping is a trap and takes that ordinary, slow, human step? 'Nero's prediction was perfect. That was why it failed. It predicted the Sora who had already panicked.' Burst's storyboarders understand pacing on a fundamental level.

posts.author: Andreas_VectorUplink
posts.body: Klaus saying 'I'm calling in Nova so that egg doesn't destroy the damn continent'... NOVA IS BACK NEXT WEEK!! Remember her quote in Ep 1 about moral standing? Peak hype!

posts.author: StormWallTheory

posts.author: EchoDesmond_Loyalist

posts.author: SoraGauthier_Fanboy

posts.author: ImageboardGoblin

posts.author: GraysonRothenbergStan
posts.body: The whole sequence with the cart flying through the sky! Grayson white-knuckling the steering bar, Sora latching his red-white MetaCode threads onto the front axle to keep it level, Ben drilling through smoke, and Minko waving her scythe... Studio Burst created the most absurd yet epic war chariot in anime!

posts.author: ShadowToast

It's not comedic relief — you feel the raw momentum, grit, and tenacity of him refusing to stay down.

posts.author: GraysonSus_NotSus
posts.body: Miyuki Sawashiro's ED '24 Hours Everyday' showing Abigail's peaceful school routine vs her bleeding in the game... tears in my eyes. Such a beautiful, nostalgic song ;_;

posts.author: AbigailFlameRush
posts.body: Ben didn't even try to dodge at the end. At 96% heat, he literally ran straight through overlapping blast zones, ate the explosion point-blank with sparks and blood flying everywhere, and rammed that spinning NodeCore drill right through Maxino's guard roaring 'HERE'S YOUR L!'

posts.author: Klaus_DeadpanEnjoyer
posts.body: Sora and Abigail reaching out for each other, their fingertips missing by two centimeters, and then the screen flashes white and EVERYONE GETS SUCKED IN?? Every single UI card reading SIGNAL LOST at once!

posts.author: ArthurWhiteCommander
posts.body: Kana Hanazawa and Saori Hayami giving the performances of their careers. When Abigail caught Zantenzetsuken between both Flame Gun frames, slid inside Miyuki's guard, and delivered that heavy spin-kick that made Miyuki's forearm visibly shake from adrenaline and pain?! That's the first time Miyuki's perfect ice-queen composure broke!

posts.author: NeroRouteMaster
posts.body: Look at the weight in Sora's landing when Ben launches him in — he hits the ground, tucks into a combat roll, pushes right back up to his feet without losing speed, and charges Nero head-on. Sora's scrappy physical combat style is so satisfying to watch!

posts.author: Zantenzetsuken_Cutter
posts.body: Maxino was such a cool boss design. The firework cylinders strapped to his rig, throwing smoke canisters and using gold blast zones to launch Ben into traps... but Ben turning the launch blast into aerial momentum with Flight Mode was galaxy-brain play.

posts.author: Grayson_Ignition_DualBlades
posts.body: Kagura holding back the Crucible flames until the very end — hands and kicks win the space, Crucibles cash out the damage! That Red Divide cut splitting the corridor in two with that delayed three-frame impact hold... Kagura is an animation god.

posts.author: EmikoFashionQueen

posts.author: CipherCaramel_Cyberpunk
posts.body: Lisa Hoshino vs Echo Desmond was the most stylish, petty catfight of the decade. Lisa's internal monologue: 'Don't shoot the person. Shoot the step they need.' followed by interrupting Margo's sound cannon with 'You're mine, pig!!' — Rina Satou at her absolute best.

posts.author: ToonblockKid

posts.author: EmikoFashionQueen
posts.body: Action Director Kagura completely reinvented anime swordplay in Grayson vs IgniteCOD_Clutch. Look at the keyframes: when Ignite tries to slide, Grayson doesn't swing a sword — he drops his hips and stamps a stiff low kick into the knee! Then a lead jab to check the SMG reload, and that brutal axe kick crashing down straight through the build panel! It's actual boxing and Muay Thai mechanics instead of floaty anime sword-flailing!

posts.author: StormWallTheory
posts.body: Action Director Kagura completely reinvented anime swordplay in Grayson vs IgniteCOD_Clutch. Look at the keyframes: when Ignite tries to slide, Grayson doesn't swing a sword — he drops his hips and stamps a stiff low kick into the knee! Then a lead jab to check the SMG reload, and that brutal axe kick crashing down straight through the build panel! It's actual boxing and Muay Thai mechanics instead of floaty anime sword-flailing!
